Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Sources indicate that matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”.

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8.

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

Sources indicate that “It was an outstanding performance,” the manager remarked. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”.

It has been revealed that the win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

Sources indicate that as for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a latest look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

Recent findings suggest that when Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”.

According to recent reports, good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Industry observers note that today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

#106527. Real Madrid attacker agrees contract until 2031 despite starting just twice under Mourinho

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (812 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Real Madrid attacker agrees contract until 2031 despite starting just twice under Mourinho

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (812 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 15:39.
  • Real Madrid are reportedly preparing to secure the future of an out-of-favour attacker with an extraordinary £880m release clause, despite his limited involvement under Jose Mourinho this season.
  • Morocco international Brahim Diaz is said to have agreed a fresh contract until June 2031, potentially extending his stay at the Santiago Bernabeu by another four years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 15:39.

Real Madrid are reportedly preparing to secure the future of an out-of-favour attacker with an extraordinary £880m release clause, despite his limited involvement under Jose Mourinho this season.

Morocco international Brahim Diaz is said to have agreed a fresh contract until June 2031, potentially extending his stay at the Santiago Bernabeu by another four years.

According to Spanish television programme El Chiringuito, the agreement includes a €1bn (£880m) release clause, with an official announcement expected next week.

Journalist Marcos Benito claims the 27-year-old signed the extension approximately two weeks ago, although Madrid have yet to confirm the arrangement publicly.

The reported deal is particularly striking given Brahim's position in Mourinho's squad, where he has struggled to secure regular opportunities despite contributing three assists this season.

His long-term future may be approaching a resolution, but his immediate prospects of becoming a first-team regular appear considerably less certain.

Brahim's existing agreement is due to expire in June 2027, making his future a subject of considerable speculation during the opening months of the campaign.

Real Madrid have been working to retain the versatile attacker, who returned from a three-year loan spell at AC Milan in 2023 and has provided valuable attacking depth in recent seasons.

However, he has found opportunities increasingly difficult to secure since Mourinho took charge.

The former Manchester City youngster has made nine appearances across all competitions in 2026-27, starting only twice and accumulating just 249 minutes of playing time.

His average of fewer than 28 minutes per appearance underlines the limited nature of his involvement, while he has started the last 11 matches on the bench.

Brahim has nevertheless contributed three assists, demonstrating that he can still influence matches during relatively brief appearances.

Competition for attacking positions has become particularly demanding.

Arda Guler has established himself as a more prominent member of Mourinho's aims, while Jude Bellingham and summer signing Yan Diomande occupy vital roles in Madrid's attacking structure.

Vinicius Junior's anticipated return from suspension and Rodrygo's recovery from injury could further complicate Brahim's attempts to secure additional minutes.

The situation has already prompted questions about his future.

Earlier this month, Sports Mole reported on Brahim's prolonged spell among the substitutes and the growing concerns surrounding his lack of playing time.

Despite those difficulties, Mourinho has reportedly supported the club's efforts to retain the Morocco international.

The proposed extension would strengthen Madrid's contractual position considerably, although a release clause of €1bn should not be interpreted as a realistic valuation or asking price.

Such figures are frequently included in contracts at major Spanish clubs to provide protection against unwanted departures.

There is, however, some uncertainty surrounding the precise duration of Brahim's new deal.

While El Chiringuito reports an agreement until 2031, Spanish newspaper AS has suggested that his renewal is arranged until 2030.

Neither version has been officially confirmed by Real Madrid.

Securing a upcoming contract would represent a significant commitment from Madrid, but it would not guarantee Brahim a more substantial role in the team.

His position is particularly intriguing given that the club have several established attacking options and continue to develop younger players competing for similar positions.

For Brahim, the challenge is to turn occasional contributions into a more consistent place in Mourinho's starting XI.

That question also has implications for Morocco, where the midfielder remains an important international despite his restricted opportunities in Spain.

The Atlas Lions are building towards the 2030 World Cup, which Morocco will co-host alongside Spain and Portugal.

National team coach Mohamed Ouahbi has previously expressed a desire to see his players become more influential at club level, while acknowledging Brahim's ability to make a difference for his country.

Former Morocco international Mustapha Hadji has taken a stronger position, publicly questioning whether such limited club involvement is compatible with regular international selection.

Brahim's reported extension therefore raises an obvious sporting dilemma.

Remaining at the Bernabeu offers the prospect of competing for major trophies and retaining his place at one of Europe's most prestigious clubs.

However, the attacking competition that has restricted him to just two starts this season is unlikely to disappear simply because his contractual future is secured.

The deal would also make a potential departure more complicated, with interested clubs likely to require negotiations with Madrid rather than having the opportunity to sign him as a free agent next summer.

There is no indication that Brahim has asked to leave, and his reported decision to extend his contract suggests that he remains committed to fighting for his place.

For Mourinho, the challenge is different: finding sufficient opportunities for a talented squad player whom Madrid appear determined to retain for the long term.

An official announcement could settle the uncertainty surrounding Brahim's contract, but his limited involvement on the pitch remains a separate glitch that the newly introduced agreement cannot resolve.

#106524. Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (3002 w)

Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3002 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that twisting two atomic layers produces a geometric moiré pattern but bonding-induced interfacial reconstruction fundamentally transforms this into an ordered dislocation network—a distinction obscured in weakly bonded van der Waals systems.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that twisting two atomic layers produces a geometric moiré pattern but bonding-induced interfacial reconstruction fundamentally transforms this into an ordered dislocation network—a distinction obscured in weakly bonded van der Waals systems. Although in-plane topological vortex nanostructures arising from twisting-induced lateral strain modulation have been linked to periodic moiré patterns in freestanding perovskite layers1,2,3 and 2D bilayers4, their coupling to the interfacial dislocation network in twisted layers remains unresolved. Here we demonstrate that twisted freestanding SrTiO3 (STO) layers undergo interfacial reconstruction into a network of screw dislocations, accompanied by the emergence of in-plane topological vortices. Unlike in previous reports, these vortices are associated with the dislocation network rather than with geometric moiré patterns. Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) reveals a beam deflection texture in registry with the interfacial dislocation network. A machine learning interatomic potential, trained on first-principles calculations, together with phase-field modelling, confirms that competing strains within the dislocation network stabilize polar vortex–antivortex pairs; first-principles calculations further reveal the emergence of an electronic superlattice with a well-defined periodicity. Our results establish twist-controlled dislocation networks as a new and versatile route to designing local polar and electronic structures in oxide materials.

  • Unai Emery has confirmed that Matty Cash is one of three Aston Villa players who will miss Saturday's Premier League fixture against Sunderland.
  • Despite the Spaniard receiving rave reviews in recent months, Villa return from the November international break on a four-match winless streak.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 20 Nov 2026 16:12.

Unai Emery has confirmed that Matty Cash is one of three Aston Villa players who will miss Saturday's Premier League fixture against Sunderland.

Despite the Spaniard receiving rave reviews in recent months, Villa return from the November international break on a four-match winless streak.

Twice giving up a two-goal lead at Manchester United in their most recent game has left Villa in 10th place in the Premier League table.

With a Champions League showdown at Galatasaray to come on Tuesday, Emery must find a balance when naming his starting lineup for the game with the Black Cats.

Speaking at a press conference on Friday, Emery revealed that Cash would not be available.

While on international duty with Poland, Cash suffered a concussion during the fixture with Romania.

Meanwhile, Matteo Ruggeri and Amadou Onana - who signed a fresh contract earlier this week - are also missing.

Emery told reporters: "The players, more or less, they are good. Not so many changes with the players [out] injured.

"Of course, [Matty] Cash is [out with] concussion and Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri they are both still out.

"Other players - they are ready.".

Although there was no mention of Aaron Wan-Bissaka after his recent injury, the expectation is that the Congo DR right-back will deputise for Cash.

Despite their exit from the EFL Cup, Villa still face a schedule that sees them playing seven times between November 21 and December 13.

Following the Sunderland and Galatasaray double-header, the West Midlands outfit play Ipswich Town, Everton, Crystal Palace, Paris Saint-Germain and Coventry City.

#106517. Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (952 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The president of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), Franz Reindl, declared shortly after the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Friday, that he had called a meeting of its main decision-making body for Monday and Tuesday.
  • Sources indicate that the Lausanne-based court had ruled that the IIHF must allow Russian national teams to take part in ice hockey world championships again.
  • "Our task now is to implement this ruling responsibly," mentioned Germany's Reindl, who was elected IIHF president just last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The president of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), Franz Reindl, declared shortly after the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Friday, that he had called a meeting of its main decision-making body for Monday and Tuesday.

Sources indicate that the Lausanne-based court had ruled that the IIHF must allow Russian national teams to take part in ice hockey world championships again. They had been barred from doing so since shortly after Russia introduced its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

"Our task now is to implement this ruling responsibly," mentioned Germany's Reindl, who was elected IIHF president just last month.

"Several championships are only weeks away, and changes to participation affect many people; players, teams, organizing committees and host cities," he noted. "We will work closely with all of them to find practical solutions.".

In a recent development, the first tournament the CAS decision applies to is the World Juniors, to be held beginning on December 26 in Canada. Just how it will affect the tournament is not clear. Hockey Canada remarked it was in contact with the IIHF and had briefed Prime Minister Mark Carney's government on the decision.

Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand told public broadcaster CBC that she is "not comfortable" with allowing a Russian team to take part in the tournament in Alberta.

"This is a very unwelcome decision given the geopolitical situation, given the actions of Russia," she remarked. "All options are on the table, and I will say, again, I greet this decision with great disappointment.".

Canada's secretary of state for sport, Adam van Koeverden, appeared to rule out Russian athletes being granted visas for the tournament.

"Canada will maintain restrictions on the participation of Russian athletes at events hosted in Canada that receive funding from the Government of Canada and explore further options to ensure that the Russian government is held accountable," he noted in a statement.

Germany is also considering its options as it prepares to host the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in Gelsenkirchen, Düsseldorf and Mannheim in May.

"The German government takes a very critical view of the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport, a government spokesman remarked on Sunday, according to the DPA news agency.

"The German government will discuss possible consequences of the ruling, including for the 2027 Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany, with the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) promptly.".

Recent findings suggest that the DEB's chief executive, Frank Lutz, is to travel to Berlin to discuss the matter with government officials this week. Speaking on broadcaster MagentaSport on the weekend, he conceded that surrendering Germany's hosting rights for the lucrative tournament was a possibility.

"I do not want to paint a black picture. I do not want to call the World Championship into question either. But of course, we at the DEB also have to consider the option of handing back this championship," he noted.

Several other national ice hockey federations have expressed disappointment at the CAS decision, including those of Ukraine, Sweden, Finland, and Czechia.

The International Olympic Committee opened the door for Russian athletes to return to international competition when it lifted its ban of the Russian Olympic Committee in July. However, the IIHF had already decided to continue to exclude Russian teams for the 2026-27 season – over security concerns. The CAS decision – handed down after an appeal by Russia – found this reasoning was insufficiently proven.

The Kremlin's reaction to the ruling was, unsurprisingly, positive.

"Russia is returning to world hockey. This place rightfully belongs to us, and discrimination in hockey has been brought to an end," Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyarev told state television channel Vesti.

A boycott of the World Juniors, Men's World Championships or other tournaments by individual nations is now emerging as a real possibility.

"We are currently working to bring as many countries as possible into a united front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia under these circumstances," Finnish Ice Hockey Association boss Heikki Hietanen stated in a statement released on the organization's website on Monday evening.

"Our stance is that we will not play against Russia as long as the war of aggression against Ukraine continues," added Hietanen, who is also a member of the IIHF Council.

By Tuesday afternoon, the Finland-led effort was gaining steam, with Sweden, Norway and Denmark making similar statements.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," Swedish Ice Hockey Federation boss Anders Larsson said in a statement.

This came shortly after Norway said it would not play Russia at the Men's World Championship and the Danish Ice Hockey Federation issued a similar statement on its website.

"Denmark will – based on the current situation and the information available to us today – not play against Russia at the World Championship in Germany in May 2027," it read. Denmark did not qualify for the World Juniors tournament.

There has been the suggestion, that having won this victory at the CAS, Russia's next focus could be on football, where its national and club teams remain excluded from international competitions.

Russian FA general secretary Maxim Mitrofanov told state news agency Tass that there "should be one rule for all.".

World football's governing body FIFA allowed a Russia boys' team to play under its national flag in the inaugural Under-15 World Cup and Festival in Azerbaijan, which kicked off last week and ends on Saturday.

This article was originally published on November 2, 2026. It was updated on November 3 with the statement from the Finnish Ice Hockey Association. It was later updated with the statements from the Swedish, Norwegian and Danish federations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Koni De Winter spoke at an event at the AC Milan store today, and he covered numerous topics with a lot of openness.

This season, De Winter has found himself in a new, key light. Matteo Gabbia spent most of pre-season in the middle of the back three, but injuries have prevented him from playing much of a role in the campaign.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Sources indicate that it’s an unfortunate shame and there may have been some worries about De Winter taking on this role. However, he’s taken the opportunity in his stride, looking every part a starter in Ruben Amorim’s defence.

Rumours about a new defender arriving will persist, so it’ll be interesting to see what happens with his minutes from January onwards. However, he’s created something of a headache, but it’s a good one to have.

Speaking to SportMediaset on the sidelines of the Meet&Greet at the Milan Store in San Babila, via MilanNews, De Winter looked at the rise in his playing time, Amorim’s closeness to the group and much more.

You also took over at Reggio Emilia when Gabbia was unfortunately injured. You’re practically always there; what does that mean to you?

“I’m playing a lot, it’s great to be playing. We’re playing a lot, and these days you train more on taking care of your body, keeping healthy, and right now I’m doing that more, but it’s great to be playing a lot of games. Playing a lot of games for Milan, and it’s even better to win games.”.

It’s all great, but it wasn’t a given: you’ve earned this place as leader. Do you now feel like a leader of this AC Milan?

It has been revealed that “I feel good at this Milan club, and as I always say, I try to give what I can. It’s also true that I might have a more key position this year. That might be true, but I always try to do my part, give my all, and help my teammates.”.

Sources indicate that it’s clear, evident, that Amorim holds you in high regard, but what is Amorim like? An adjective.

Recent findings suggest that “I’d say he’s very human. He’s one of us, he laughs, he has fun, but when he has to be serious, he’s serious. He lives with the group, the group feels close to him, and I think that gives the players a good feeling. It’s nice to work for him and with him.”.

Is it true that he got very angry after the defeat against Ferencvaros?

“Yes, but I think the whole group felt that we had played a very poor game, so, as I saw it, my teammates saw it too.”.

Sources indicate that are Ferencvaros and Bologna two games you’re ready to say “never again” to? Will Frosinone be a different team?

“Yes, exactly, as I said, we are very confident, but sometimes even too much so, and then all matches are difficult against whoever we play against, and we have to understand this swiftly and we can’t make the same mistakes.”.

It has been revealed that among the various critics, it’s remarked that this AC Milan team has enormous potential, but there are too many ups and downs. Does it need more consistency?

“Yes, I think it hurts even more when we lose because we know we can do well, we can win every game. So yes, when we really lose, in the locker room you feel like we’ve let ourselves down first and then everyone else.”.

You recently became the father of a beautiful baby girl. What are your nights like as a dad?

Industry observers note that “At night, I’m fine. My girlfriend is working really hard, so it’s a lot for me. I mean, I get up sometimes, but it’s much quieter. I think it’s harder for her.”.

And how much has life changed with the arrival of a daughter?

Sources indicate that “It’s changed a lot, I mean, I don’t know how to explain it. When you’re at work, you think about your daughter, you want to come home earlier, you want to hold her, you want her – I mean, you have more beautiful moments – but it’s hard to explain. I don’t know how to explain it.”.

You were also used as a full-back, but now you only play as a centre-back….

“Good, good, because I also consider myself a centre-back, but it’s true that I can also play full-back. It’s something I can do, but it’s not my favourite position. But yes, it’s true that I’ve played a few games there in the past, but I’m happy playing as a centre back and I’m happy that the coach sees that too.”.

Sources indicate that “I mean, crazy in a good way, yes. He likes to have fun, he likes to dance, he likes to talk, so he’s a bright spot, as they say, for the locker room, yes.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Well, that’s a good question. Yes, I miss her. I thought about it even when the little girl was born: I also want to score a goal, I mean, dedicate a goal to her, so I miss her, yes.”.

How do you concentrate when you’re in the hotel retreat? How do you focus in the hours leading up to kick-off?

“It’s become a routine now, so I always do the same things. You’re in the hotel, you take a shower, you play a little video game or you’re on your phone, so now I don’t even think about it, it’s really become a routine.”.

What does Maignan ask of you, defenders?

“He states to stay focused on the game because, as we know, one moment can change the game and at Milan it can also change a season, so it’s very key not to underestimate every moment and always stay focused.

It seems to me that there is a great understanding between you and Strahinja Pavlovic even off the pitch….

“Yes, it’s true, he and I have a good relationship; we met last year. Then when you see him you might not think, I mean, I didn’t think he would be such a great friend, but we got along really well both on and off the pitch, it’s really nice to spend time with him.”.

Industry observers note that our 007s at Milanello tell us about some great ping pong matches between you and Pavlovic. Who’s the better player?

Sources indicate that “This is difficult, but he started at a much higher level than me. But now I’ve improved a lot, although I have to say he’s even stronger. But yes, every day we start with a game of ping pong and then we start working.”.

Would you like your daughter to play soccer in the future? Are you planning a second child? Would you like to have a son who plays soccer?

Recent findings suggest that “I want her to do what she wants, where she feels good, where she doesn’t feel pressured, and where she can express herself best. And then, going back to ping pong, I think there’s some video; maybe we can see me beat her.”.

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 16:27, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 16:39.

Liverpool duo Virgil van Dijk and Dominik Szoboszlai are both good to go for Sunday's Premier League clash with Manchester United at Anfield.

The pair were name-checked as part of Andoni Iraola's six-man injury revision, in which he confirmed that the Hungarian midfielder and Dutch defender are both fine to feature despite fitness concerns.

Szoboszlai has been managing a knee issue recently, but there is nothing to suggest that he will not join forces with Alexis Mac Allister in central midfield, even though Ryan Gravenberch could also return from a heel injury.

Van Dijk, meanwhile, withdrew from the Netherlands squad during the November international break, but the 35-year-old will no doubt partner Jeremy Jacquet in front of Alisson Becker here.

Fellow Dutchman Jeremie Frimpong is also in line to return from a hamstring injury, but Ronald Araujo has done nothing to warrant demotion, and nor has Milos Kerkez on the left-hand side.

Scorer of five goals against Manchester United in the Premier League, Cody Gakpo enjoys facing the Red Devils more than any other Premier League team and is a sure-fire starter on the right flank.

Expect Gakpo to line up alongside Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak in an unchanged forward line, the latter bidding to build on his seven goals from nine Premier League games so far in 2026-27.

Liverpool possible starting lineup:.

Alisson; Araujo, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Gakpo, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak.

  • Mudryk, now on loan at Tottenham from Chelsea, was suspended for 20 months between November 2024 and July 2026 after testing positive for banned substance meldonium in October 2024.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 16:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 18:30 EST, 19 November 2026.

Andriy Shevchenko has accused Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives of trying to persuade the Ukrainian FA to find someone to falsely take the blame for the winger's failed drugs test.

Mudryk, now on loan at Tottenham from Chelsea, was suspended for 20 months between November 2024 and July 2026 after testing positive for banned substance meldonium in October 2024.

In an interview, Mudryk blamed the Ukrainian FA (UAF), claiming the substance entered his body while on international duty.

'This drug could only have got into my body where I was, and that's Ukraine,' he remarked.

But Shevchenko, president of the UAF, described the accusations as 'baseless slander'. Shevchenko added: 'His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample,' he told Tribuna. 'Such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work.'.

Shevchenko said investigations had failed to establish how the substance entered Mudryk's system. He added that national team staff complied with Chelsea's request not to give Mudryk medication, and that two of his personal specialists were allowed at training camps.

Mykhailo Mudryk (left) has been accused of 'baseless slander' by Ukraine FA (UAF) president Andriy Shevchenko after he blamed his failed drugs test on the national team's setup.

'If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it,' Shevchenko noted, demanding a public retraction and apology otherwise.

Mudryk's representatives have been approached for comment.

According to recent reports, the 25-year-old was initially handed a four-year ban after being charged by the Football Association for failing a doping test. He was able to return when a seismic resolution was struck after changes to the 'scientific reporting standards'.

In a bombshell two-hour interview with Ukrainian journalist Dmitry Gordon via his YouTube channel, Mudryk laid the blame for his situation with the Ukraine national team - something Shevchenko vehemently denies.

'Loud statements have been made about the UAF and the Ukrainian national team. This is baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally,' the UAF president, who also played for Chelsea during his time, remarked in a statement to The Athletic.

'After Mykhailo became a Chelsea player, the club sent a letter to the UAF requesting that he not be given any medication during national team training camps,' he continued.

It has been revealed that 'The national team staff complied with this request. Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps. These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine.

Mudryk has won 28 caps for Ukraine but is yet to represent them since his ban was overturned.

Recent findings suggest that 'The UAF completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk's representatives with the information they requested and remained in contact with those working on the case.

'I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism. If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question.'.

In his interview, Mudryk - who is yet to add to his 28 caps for his country since returning from his ban - laid the blame at Ukraine's door.

'I had never heard of a drug like meldonium, never seen it, never come across it in my life. I only learned about it when they told me the news. I definitely have ideas. It's a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe,' the winger said.

Industry observers note that 'This drug could only have got into my body where I was, and that's Ukraine. There are no such drugs in England. It supposedly stimulates your heart and helps you, as far as I understand, handle physical load better.

It has been revealed that 'I was at home and Chelsea's management came to see me and they said we needed to talk. Then they say you've returned a positive doping test and now you're facing a ban.

Recent findings suggest that 'You can't believe it's true. You can't believe this is happening to you. If I'd ever taken anything anywhere, I'd have understood that this conversation might happen one day.

He is at the moment on loan at Tottenham from Chelsea but has only played once so far this season.

'At least I'd have understood it was possible. But when you spend a huge pile of money on watching your diet, on a nutritionist, on a chef. When you spend that much money every year on all these things, that's the last thing you expect. Because it speaks for itself: that you take things very seriously, like nutrition, everything that goes into your body, you watch it very closely.

'Otherwise there'd be no need to spend money on it, because you could manage without it. They tell you this news, and you sit there, and you kind of listen to them but don't hear them.

'At some point you just go into a trance. It feels like you're falling in a dream off a skyscraper. You're flying down, you feel yourself flying down, and only in a dream do you wake up when you hit the ground, but in real life you don't wake up, you just keep falling. It hits you very hard mentally. At that moment the tears came later.'.

Mudryk, who joined Chelsea for £89million from Shakhtar Donetsk, has only made one substitute appearance for Tottenham so far this season due to an ankle injury.

Search, Trends and Live Sport Specialist.

Leeds United avenged the two cup defeats they suffered at Chelsea’s hands with a stunning 4-1 victory over their old rivals at Stamford Bridge.

Having been edged out by the Blues at the semi-final stage of the FA Cup in April, Leeds were subjected to a 6-3 Carabao Cup mauling by Xabi Alonso’s men in September.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

On this occasion, however, it was Daniel Farke’s men inflicting the damage. Emmanuel Emegha fired the hosts ahead, but Noah Okafor goals either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty and a late Brenden Aaronson finish gave Leeds a Premier League win that will go down in the history books.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea sought to assume authority from the get-go, with Cole Palmer driving at the heart of the Leeds midfield inside the opening minute. The hosts may have been straight on the offensive, but Leeds soon made it clear they would not be content with one-way traffic.

Jayden Bogle and Sean Longstaff both made headway down the right-hand side, sending in crosses that were not capitalised upon.

Recent findings suggest that the opening exchanges played out in a fast and furious manner, with robust challenges stoking the fires of a historic rivalry. Chelsea had the early edge, although referee Michael Oliver had no interest in appeals for a penalty when Tarik Muharemovic challenged Emmanuel Emegha inside the box.

Leeds handled Chelsea’s ventures forward well, mostly limiting the Blues to speculative efforts. Josh Acheamping, Morgan Rogers and Estevao all pulled the trigger from distance, yet little was asked of James Trafford between the Leeds sticks.

In a recent development, at the other end, Leeds continued to make inroads on the right. James Justin whipped a cross over for Calvert-Lewin, who struggled to generate power but did hit the crossbar with his looped header.

Leeds’ focus soon shifted to the left, where Gudmundsson started to flex his attacking muscles. He made an incisive dart into the box and went to ground under close attention from Estevao, although the referee paid no attention to penalty appeals.

Leeds’ left wing-back then picked out Calvert-Lewin and saw the England international force a strong hand from Emiliano Martinez with a headed effort.

The visitors looked to be moving through the gears but just as the tide was turning, Chelsea drew first blood. Justin and Nico Elvedi both failed to stop the advancement of Rogers, who fed Emegha and saw the frontman beat Trafford at his near post with a blasted finish.

Leeds bit back almost immediately, levelling proceedings within three minutes of the opener. Calvert-Lewin contested a long ball with Wesley Fofana before picking up the scraps and releasing Okafor, who jinked his way into space and rifled across Martinez.

In a recent development, with the wind behind their sails, Leeds came close to overturning the deficit via their equaliser’s creator. Calvert-Lewin met a Muharemovic cross and his deft flick came agonisingly close to finding the bottom corner.

Farke’s men continued applying pressure in the closing stages of the first half and Ao Tanaka was unfortunate to see a rasping rocket of a shot deflected before it could cause Martinez any trouble.

Gudmundsson then danced his way into an opportunity before poking harmlessly wide of Martinez’s right-hand post.

The next chance fell to Tanaka, who pushed the ball out of his feet but could only force a straightforward save with a shot straight down Martinez’s throat.

Leeds did have the ball in the back of the net on the stroke of half-time, although Justin was clearly offside before he delivered for Muharemovic to finish. When the half-time whistle did blow, it was Leeds firmly in the driving seat.

Sources indicate that the second half started as the first ended, with Leeds in the ascendency. There were early appeals for a penalty when Calvert-Lewin tangled with Martinez, but Oliver was again dismissive of protests.

Tanaka then stretched to get on the end of a cross from deep, steering just off target as pressure piled on Chelsea.

Industry observers note that having seen their protests ignored mere minutes earlier, Leeds saw Oliver point to the spot when Rogers was judged to have handled a Muharemovic shot. After a lengthy VAR check, the decision was stuck by and Calvert-Lewin buried the spot-kick.

Chelsea responded by putting their front foot forward and Rogers forced Trafford down to his left with a low drive from distance.

However, it was Leeds who struck next and sent the the travelling supporters into a frenzy. After Chelsea failed to clear their lines after a long throw, Ethan Ampadu’s deflected cross was hammered home by Okafor in emphatic fashion.

Somewhat predictably, Chelsea surged back into the driving seat as they looked for a way back into a game getting away from them. Much to the frustration of the home supporters, their spell of control yielded little more than occasional half-chances.

There were sharp inhales of breath when Rogers arrowed a free-kick goalwards from a tight angle, but it dipped over the crossbar with Trafford at full stretch.

Many of Chelsea’s supporters were already heading out to beat the traffic when Aaronson capped an astonishing afternoon, wriggling through a creaking defence before steering a fourth past Martinez.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 16:39.

Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino could recall Lisandro Martinez to his starting lineup for his opening game in charge away to Liverpool on Sunday in the Premier League.

The Argentine defender is available to his compatriot after completing a domestic suspension and could now slot back into the rearguard alongside Harry Maguire, who has seemingly shaken off a back problem.

Noussair Mazraoui would be the most likely to make way if Martinez returns, as Leny Yoro shuffles over to right-back, on the opposite side to the much-maligned Diogo Dalot.

The Portugal international's withdrawal was cheered by fans in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, but with Patrick Dorgu operating in a more attack-minded role of late and Luke Shaw still doubtful, Dalot should reprise his role.

The same goes for Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo in the middle, as Pochettino sticks to a 4-2-3-1 setup for his maiden match and forces Andrey Santos to wait his turn.

The front four of Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo is likely to remain the same too, although Marcus Rashford (hip) is on the verge of returning and could be an option on Merseyside.

Carlos Baleba (hamstring), Manuel Ugarte (knee) and Benjamin Sesko (calf) all remain out of contention for the away side.

#106502. Latest Update: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?

Latest Update: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (861 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With more than $1 trillion (€900 billion) pouring into the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout, US tech giants are now competing with governments and companies in Europe for the same investment capital.
  • It has been revealed that four of the Substantial Five hyperscalers — Amazon, Google owner Alphabet, Meta and Oracle — have issued about $250 billion in bonds in dollars since the beginning of 2025, according to a tally of filings to US financial regulators by AI Industry Reviews, an independent platform that evaluates AI tools.
  • Recently, Microsoft, the last of the Substantial Five to hold back, joined the AI borrowing spree with a $25 billion bond sale, all in dollars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With more than $1 trillion (€900 billion) pouring into the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout, US tech giants are now competing with governments and companies in Europe for the same investment capital.

It has been revealed that four of the Substantial Five hyperscalers — Amazon, Google owner Alphabet, Meta and Oracle — have issued about $250 billion in bonds in dollars since the beginning of 2025, according to a tally of filings to US financial regulators by AI Industry Reviews, an independent platform that evaluates AI tools. They have sold a further €37 billion ($41 billion) of bonds in euros.

Recently, Microsoft, the last of the Substantial Five to hold back, joined the AI borrowing spree with a $25 billion bond sale, all in dollars.

Next year, Goldman Sachs projects that total latest AI hyperscaler bond sales are expected to reach $420 billion. About €60 billion will be issued in euros, according to Dutch bank ING.

That is unwelcome news for European companies and countries like France, Germany and Italy, whose sovereign bond yields have risen sharply in recent months and are already straining public finances.

With public debt at 119% of gross domestic product (GDP) and a deficit still running above 5%, France is already paying a sizable risk premium on its debt. Over the past six months, yields on French 10-year bonds have climbed from roughly 3.7% to nearly 5%.

The French government's interest bill is set to rise from €79 billion currently to €91 billion next year and over €100 billion by 2028.

Based on these figures alone, France's Finance Ministry needs to find tens of billions of euros in additional cuts, tax hikes, or more borrowing by the end of the decade.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In August, economists at the European Central Bank mentioned the euro bond market was adapting well to the presence of AI giants but warned they "could make it harder for other companies and other economic sectors to access finance.".

Writing in a blog post, they also questioned whether the bloc's financial markets can "smoothly handle such large and concentrated debt inflows and warned of a "potential spillover to the sovereign and supranational segment of the bond market.".

That means governments and international lenders such as the European Union and the European Investment Bank could also end up paying more to borrow.

Viktor Hjort, global head of credit strategy at the French bank BNP Paribas, described the phenomenon as "bond abundance.".

Hjort told DW that the presence of the hyperscalers in the euro bond market is "already high enough to create competition" within the corporate sector and "between corporates and governments for available fixed income funds." These are investment funds that mostly buy bonds, which pay regular interest.

Bond yields jumped again last month, driven by rebounding energy prices linked to the Iran war and France’s political crisis, which Hjort noted further revealed the growing competition for capital, as government and tech giant borrowing costs rose together.

Normally, nervous investors move into government bonds during uncertain times, which pushes their borrowing costs down.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that goldman Sachs warned last week that rising interest costs were starting to hurt earnings at European companies. Among firms in the Stoxx 600 — an index of 600 large, mid-sized and small companies across Europe — Goldman found that interest costs as a share of sales have risen by nearly half since 2022.

The bank's analysts stated this had cut earnings by more than 5% over the same period.

Factor in the competition from AI bonds, and European firms could now face pressure to cut their investments in fresh plants, equipment and research, as well as shareholder payouts, to prioritize loan repayments.

According to recent reports, the pressure doesn't stop at national governments. Europe's cities and regions, whose borrowing helps to fund schools, transport and infrastructure, may also feel the effects of the AI boom.

A study for the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development(OECD), published in January, compared local bond markets in Belgium, Germany, Spain, Sweden and Canada. Where AI was spreading fastest, measured by the share of AI-related job vacancies, borrowing costs for cities and regions tended to rise.

"Whereas in the United States, my research has found that AI investments are linked to a lower cost of borrowing for municipalities, the opposite appears to hold in several European countries," the study's co-author, Christos Makridis of Arizona State University's W. P. Carey School of Business, told DW.

While AI bonds are far from the sole cause of Europe's widening fiscal strains, US Significant Tech's huge appetite for capital could add further pressure next year, due to the additional billions in newly introduced bonds planned.

The irony is that European taxpayers could end up paying more on their own governments' debt, partly to help finance an AI boom across the Atlantic.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.
  • According to recent reports, this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic.
  • Industry observers note that the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

According to recent reports, this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

Industry observers note that the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

It has been revealed that the best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

According to recent reports, “I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

According to recent reports, avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an glitch for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

It has been revealed that england thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

In a recent development, the Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

Toone promptly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

Emmanuel Emegha rifled the hosts ahead on the 25-minute mark but Leeds were back on level terms within three minutes.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Noah Okafor levelled proceedings and the Whites did not stop there, striking again through Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Okafor and Brenden Aaronson to claim an emphatic 4-1 victory.

“[It was a] great result,” said Farke. “Obviously I think the first win here at Stamford Bridge for us as a club in this century, so it says a lot about how it ranks more or less in the history books of Leeds United.

In a recent development, “[It was a] great performance. I would have been disappointed even with a draw today. I was a bit disappointed even at half-time when it was just a draw because I think we were, from the first and last, the better side.

“Somehow you concede a goal, but what I liked a lot is that we highlighted the mentality, we were not bothered. We played further on on the front foot and didn't doubt ourselves and wanted to play exactly the way we have played. I think a great reaction and also to equalise and to play further on.

“The boys came out flying and it seemed like they listened. There were some great team moves and great chances. We were then also clinical in front of the opponent's goal and could have scored perhaps even a few more, but I can't complain too much with a 4-1 win here away at Chelsea.”.

Leeds registered a staggering 21 shots against Chelsea’s star-studded side, outfighting and outclassing an expensively assembled side.

Statistics show Chelsea enjoyed the lion’s share of possession, but control was very much with the Whites.

“We dominated this game,” Farke said. “We made sure that our plan for this game works.

“We wanted to play on the front foot, we wanted to press Chelsea high, we wanted to make sure that they can't show their world-class potential.

“They have unbelievable players and we didn't want these players in the mood to enjoy the game. I still think that Chelsea came out motivated today and also played with intensity.”.

Leeds have risen to sixth in the Premier League table, leapfrogging Chelsea with the victory.

  • Serie A's Sunday night showdown will see a battle of the Nerazzurri, as Atalanta BC welcome Inter Milan to Bergamo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 20 Nov 2026 17:02, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 09:33.

Serie A's Sunday night showdown will see a battle of the Nerazzurri, as Atalanta BC welcome Inter Milan to Bergamo.

When the black-and-blue pair go toe to toe once again, the hosts hope to finally end an eight-year wait for victory over their regional rivals.

Having suffered derby defeat and slipped off top spot in Serie A, reigning champions Inter bounced back with two big wins - and a rare pair of clean sheets - before international football intervened.

Responding to their Derby della Madonnina loss to old foes AC Milan, the Nerazzurri recorded a crucial Champions League victory against Feyenoord, then extended their long reign of dominance over Como.

The visitors were flying high following their own European exploits, but Inter put in a commanding display while posting a 15th consecutive Serie A home win over the Lariani.

Though surprise leaders Lazio finally dropped points, that was not quite enough to reclaim the summit, and Cristian Chivu's side went into the break sandwiched between both Rome clubs.

Now, they return to action with an important double-header, at home to Stuttgart in the Champions League and against Atalanta this weekend.

After nine consecutive away wins helped them secure the Scudetto last season, Inter's form on the road has recently faltered - relatively speaking, at least.

Nonetheless, the second-city giants have prevailed on all of their last four trips to Bergamo, averaging two goals per game.

In fact, Atalanta are winless across the last 15 league meetings at any venue, while also suffering defeats in the cup and Supercoppa Italiana.

Even during the golden Gian Piero Gasperini era, La Dea struggled to conquer Inter, picking up just two points from the last seven clashes on home turf.

This time, the pair will convene with Atalanta trailing far behind their Lombardy neighbours, languishing inside the bottom half of Serie A.

A 1-0 win over Monza somewhat steadied the ship ahead of the international break, after losing half of their first 10 league fixtures under Maurizio Sarri.

It also halted a streak of 11 games without a clean sheet, including in the Conference League, where the Bergamaschi only sit 16th halfway through the league phase.

Sarri's side have conceded the third-most shots in Italy's top tier, and already shipping 20 goals by this stage of a campaign represents Atalanta's worst defensive start since 2002.

All of which makes for grim reading ahead of Inter's visit to New Balance Arena, where the hosts have registered just four wins from nine games this term.

Atalanta BC form (all competitions):.

Inter Milan form (all competitions):.

Inter star Lautaro Martinez has scored in five of his last six league games against Atalanta, and he is set to return from an injury layoff on Sunday evening; only Aleksandar Stankovic and Ange Bonny are currently sidelined.

In his captain's absence, Marcus Thuram certainly stepped up, and a recent strike against Como took the French forward onto six Serie A goals for the season.

Pio Esposito also found the net in that match, ending a domestic drought that dated back to September; then, he hit the target twice before missing a penalty for Italy during an eventful international period.

Sources indicate that like Esposito, Atalanta's Nikola Krstovic scored in a 1-1 draw when these sides last met. The Montenegro striker is now in top form: the winner against Monza was his seventh league goal of the season, and he has just scored three times in two UEFA Nations League matches.

La Dea's injury list features three defenders - Isak Hien, Odilon Kossounou and Thomas Kristensen - while midfielder Gianluca Gaetano remains a doubt.

More positively for Sarri, ex-Inter man Raoul Bellanova and Italy forward Giacomo Raspadori are both back in contention after recovering from thigh problems.

Atalanta BC possible starting lineup:.

Carnesecchi; Bellanova, Scalvini, Kolasinac, Zappacosta; Ederson, Kessie; Elmas, De Ketelaere, Rowe; Krstovic.

Inter Milan possible starting lineup:.

J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Bastoni; Spence, Barella, Calhanoglu, Sucic, Dimarco; Thuram, Esposito.

Inter have attempted the most shots in Serie A this season, they last failed to score in March, and their prolific talisman is set to make his long-awaited comeback.

That could mean trouble for Atalanta's fragile defence, so the hosts will suffer yet another defeat to their Nerazzurro neighbours.

Latest Update: Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 43 min read (8611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~43 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, one active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p-wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs.
  • Unconventional symmetry breaking in itinerant fermion systems has revealed some of the most remarkable phases of quantum matter.
  • Recently, spin group theory has provided a framework for identifying such magnetic states5, extending concepts developed for altermagnets12.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, one active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p-wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs. 1,2,3). Achieving p-wave superconductivity4 and its magnetic analogue5—characterized by a time-reversal-symmetric, p-wave spin-polarized Fermi surface—remains a grand challenge6,7. Despite recent progress in identifying candidate p-wave magnets5,7,8,9,10, spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for their electronic structures remains limited. Here we report angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-ARPES evidence for p-wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, supported by symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and neutron scattering. Neutron diffraction reveals a chiral spiral phase between 33.4 K and 62 K that fulfils archetypal p-wave magnetism criteria: it preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, while breaking inversion symmetry. Spin-integrated ARPES reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, and spin-ARPES resolves Sy polarization in near-Fermi-level spectral features. The extracted Sy exhibits a sign-changing modulation across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p-wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Magnetic force microscopy and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-μm chiral magnetic domains. These results identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p-wave magnetism in electronic band structures and spin-symmetry-based functionalities in spintronics10, topological matter7, superconductivity11 and beyond.

Unconventional symmetry breaking in itinerant fermion systems has revealed some of the most remarkable phases of quantum matter. A celebrated example is p-wave superfluidity in helium-3, where odd-parity Cooper pairing generates emergent orders beyond conventional paradigms1,2,3. Its magnetic analogue, the p-wave magnet, is characterized by an odd-parity spin-polarized electronic structure that preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation while breaking inversion symmetry5,6.

Recently, spin group theory has provided a framework for identifying such magnetic states5, extending concepts developed for altermagnets12. Whereas ferromagnets exhibit conventional s-wave-like spin splitting and altermagnets exhibit even-parity d-, g- or i-wave spin order12,13, p-wave magnets are characterized by odd-parity spin polarization associated with commensurate coplanar magnetic order that breaks inversion symmetry while preserving a combined time-reversal and translation symmetry5,14. The resulting electronic structure can exhibit a single symmetry-allowed spin component, symmetry-enforced nodal planes and a characteristic momentum-dependent spin texture. Candidate p-wave magnetism has recently been explored in insulating NiI2 (ref. 8) and metallic Gd3(Ru1−δRhδ)4Al12 (ref. 9). However, spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for the characteristic odd-parity electronic spin texture remains limited8,9.

In a recent development, here we present evidence for p-wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level (near-EF) electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi by combining symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations, neutron scattering and photoemission spectroscopy. Neutron diffraction reveals a commensurate spiral phase with propagation vector (0, 1/3, 0) below the upper magnetic transition temperature, TN1 ≈ 62 K, followed by a transition to a conical phase at the lower magnetic transition temperature, TN2 ≈ 33.4 K. Magnetotransport measurements indicate strong coupling between magnetism and itinerant electrons. Below TN1, spin-integrated angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, associated with strong 4f–5d exchange coupling. Spin-ARPES provides spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for the expected odd-parity Sy polarization in the near-EF spectral features: the extracted polarization changes sign across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p-wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Because the near-EF spin-resolved features contain contributions from multiple folded bands with momentum-dependent spectral weights, the observed Sy modulation is best interpreted as a spectroscopic signature of the expected p-wave spin texture at the level of the reconstructed electronic structure. Magnetic force microscopy (MFM) and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-µm chiral magnetic domains. Together, these observations identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p-wave magnetism in electronic band structures and related spin-symmetry-based phenomena.

According to recent reports, in conventional ferromagnets and altermagnets (Fig. 1a), broken time-reversal symmetry permits even-parity spin-polarized electronic structures12. In the non-relativistic limit, conventional ferromagnets exhibit s-wave-like spin splitting, whereas altermagnets can exhibit d-, g- or i-wave-like spin-splitting patterns12,13,15,16,17,18. By contrast, unconventional odd-parity magnets can host p-, f- or h-wave spin polarization that preserves time-reversal (\(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}\))-related symmetry while breaking inversion (\(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{P}}\)) symmetry5. Commensurate chiral magnetic structures provide a natural route to such \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{P}}\)-symmetry breaking. In particular, coplanar non-collinear exchange fields can generate odd-parity spin polarization in momentum space when the magnetic structure preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}{\boldsymbol{\tau }}\) (ref. 5). As in conventional antiferromagnets, this symmetry enforces zero net magnetization in the ideal p-wave magnetic state (Fig. 1a).

Magenta and cyan spheres represent magnetic atoms with opposite spin orientations, related by the indicated combined spin–space symmetry operations in the d- and p-wave states, whereas blue spheres represent nonmagnetic atoms. b, Spiral magnetic structure of EuSi. The characteristic p-wave spin group symmetries are spin rotation combined with a glide mirror plane \([{C}_{2z}{||}{M}_{y}{\bf{t}}]\), and with a lattice translation \([{C}_{2}{||}{\bf{t}}]\), respectively. c, Calculated spin-polarized Fermi surface of the spiral phase, including SOC, showing p-wave spin polarization and spin splitting. d, Calculated spin textures near the top of the valence bands in the kz = 0 (bottom) and kx = 0 (top) planes, with (left) and without (right) SOC. e, Calculated spin-polarized band dispersion along the −Ym–Г–Ym (ky) direction in the spiral phase, with (left) and without (right) SOC. f, Conical magnetic structure of EuSi, with the combined spin-rotation and translation symmetry \([{C}_{6}{||}{{\bf{t}}}^{{\prime} }]\) indicated. g, Calculated spin-polarized band dispersions along the same momentum direction in the conical phase, with (left) and without (right) SOC.

We next consider the symmetry of the experimentally determined magnetic structures of EuSi. The crystal belongs to the point group D2h (space group Cmcm), and its magnetic states without (with) considering the effect of spin–orbit coupling (SOC) are described by the corresponding spin (magnetic) space group7. For the spiral state below TN1 ≈ 62 K, the spin space group is \({{}^{{2}_{y}}C}^{1}{m}^{{m}_{x}}{c}^{1}{m}^{{m}_{y}}1\), which satisfies the criteria for collinear p-wave spin polarization in momentum space. The spin space group breaks the \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{P}}\) symmetry, thereby allowing odd-parity spin polarization. The coplanarity of the magnetic moments, together with the spin-only symmetry \({C}_{2y}{\mathcal{T}}=[{M}_{y}|1]\,{=}^{{m}_{y}}1\), constrains the spin polarization to the y direction in momentum space. Combined with the \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}{\boldsymbol{\tau }}\) symmetry, the spin group symmetry prohibits the spin components Sx and Sz, while allowing a \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}\)-symmetric Sy component satisfying:.

Recent findings suggest that the spin-degenerate nodal plane at ky = 0, where ky is the component of the electron crystal momentum k = (kx, ky, kz) along the reciprocal-space direction corresponding to the crystallographic b axis, is protected by the combined spin rotation, lattice mirror and translation symmetry \([{C}_{2z}{||}{M}_{y}t]\), as illustrated in Fig. 1b. The corresponding spin-polarized electronic-structure calculations are shown in Fig. 1c–e. Figure 1d illustrates the calculated p-wave spin–momentum locking near the top of the valence band in the (kx, ky, 0) and (0, ky, kz) planes. The calculated bands obey the symmetry relations:.

Here, E(kx,ky,kz,Sy) denotes the electronic band energy at crystal momentum k for a state with spin polarization Sy along the b direction. Comparison of calculations with and without SOC (Fig. 1c–e) demonstrates that the characteristic p-wave spin polarization and splitting arise predominantly from the non-relativistic magnetic exchange, with only minor modifications from SOC. These calculations therefore provide the symmetry and electronic-structure framework for the p-wave state expected from the spin and magnetic (\({P}_{C}{2}_{1}{2}_{1}{2}_{1}\)) space groups of the experimentally determined spiral magnetic structure.

We next consider the conical state below TN2 ≈ 33.4 K. Its spin space group takes the ferromagnetic form \({{}^{{2}_{y}}C}^{1}{m}^{{m}_{x}}{c}^{1}{m}^{{6}_{y}}{t}^{{\prime} }\), characterized by a symmetry combining a six-fold spin rotation with translation, [\({C}_{6y}{|}{t}^{{\prime} }\)], as shown in Fig. 1f. Figure 1g demonstrates the calculated electronic structure without and with SOC. The calculated dispersions of the spiral and conical phases are similar over much of momentum space but differ near the Γ point (Fig. 1e,g). In the conical phase, broken \(\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}\) lifts the spin degeneracy at the Γ point that is protected in the spiral phase (see Supplementary Note 1 for further symmetry analysis). Accordingly, an anomalous Hall response is symmetry-allowed in the conical phase but prohibited in the spiral phase. The magnetic space groups of both phases are chiral.

Sources indicate that euSi crystallizes in space group Cmcm (No. 63; Supplementary Tables 1–3). Single crystals were grown by the Bridgman method. Scanning transmission electron microscopy indicates high crystalline quality with few crystalline defects (Supplementary Fig. 2), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis yielded an Eu:Si ratio of 50.2:49.8, consistent with stoichiometric EuSi within instrumental uncertainty (Supplementary Fig. 3). Two magnetic transitions occur at TN1 ≈ 62 K and TN2 ≈ 33.4 K, together with a weak structural distortion near the structural distortion temperature TS ≈ 60 K (Supplementary Fig. 4). Magnetization measurements along the three crystallographic axes show no pronounced hysteresis (Fig. 2b and Supplementary Fig. 6), indicating the absence of net magnetic moments at zero field. Upon cooling, these phase transitions define two boundaries: from the paramagnetic to the spiral magnetic phase, and subsequently to the conical magnetic phase (discussed later). Upon applying a magnetic field along the crystal’s a, b and c axes (Fig. 1f), the conical magnetic/spiral magnetic state exhibits metamagnetic transitions associated with spin-flop processes, and eventually evolves into a spin-polarized state at high fields (Supplementary Fig. 6c,f,i). Angular-dependent susceptibility further shows a pronounced two-fold magnetic anisotropy (Supplementary Fig. 7).
